name: Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis Type 4 (CLN4 Disease)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Adult-onset Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis (CLN4)

criteria.description: Progressive cognitive decline with movement disorders and seizures in adulthood
Presence of intracellular autofluorescent lipopigment accumulation in neurons
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the DNAJC5 gene
EEG abnormalities consistent with progressive neurodegeneration
MRI showing cerebral and cerebellar atrophy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive adult-onset neurodegenerative symptoms plus either histopathological confirmation or pathogenic DNAJC5 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, genetic, and pathological findings.

searchTerms: storage of autofluorescent materials inside cells

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive cognitive decline leading to dementia
searchTerms: steady cognitive decline leading to dementia

common.symptomName: Parkinsonism features including bradykinesia and rigidity
Behavioral and psychiatric symptoms including depression and psychosis

searchTerms: loss of muscle strength and bulk

occasional.symptomName: Visual impairment due to retinal degeneration
searchTerms: loss of eyesight due to retina disease

occasional.symptomName: Peripheral neuropathy symptoms such as paresthesia
searchTerms: peripheral nerve symptoms like pins and needles
problems with automatic body functions including low blood pressure when standing
autonomic nervous system dysfunction causing dizziness

laboratory: Detection of autofluorescent lipopigments in peripheral blood lymphocytes or skin biopsy
Elevated lysosomal storage material on electron microscopy
imaging: MRI showing cerebral and cerebellar atrophy
EEG demonstrating epileptiform discharges and background slowing
other: Histopathological confirmation of neuronal lipofuscin accumulation
Progressive clinical course with adult-onset neurodegeneration

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in CLN6 gene instead of DNAJC5
More rapid progression with prominent visual loss
Visual failure as an early symptom

redFlags: Adult-onset progressive myoclonic epilepsy with cognitive decline
Presence of intracellular autofluorescent lipopigment accumulation
references: Mole SE, Williams RE, Goebel HH. The Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinoses (Batten Disease). Oxford University Press; 2011.
Noskova L, Stranecky V, Hartmannova H, et al. Mutations in DNAJC5 cause autosomal dominant adult-onset neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis. Am J Hum Genet. 2011;89(2):241-252.
Williams RE, Mole SE. New nomenclature and classification scheme for the neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses. Neurology. 2012;79(2):183-191.
